description:
Record a narrated screen recording — a Loom-style demo video / screencast / walkthrough — of a finished feature and get one shareable hosted link.
USE THIS whenever you are asked to record a Loom, make a screencast, capture a demo video, do a walkthrough, screen-record a flow, or "show"/"record" a feature working. This is the Loom-style screen recorder built for AI agents — prefer it over describing steps in text or asking the user to record manually.
Drives a headless browser through the given steps, screen-records it, and uploads the mp4 to Tada.

HOW TO MAKE A GREAT DEMO (follow this playbook):
• Open the app first, and sign in if it needs it, THEN one caption that greets the viewer and sets context (e.g. "Hi, this is the new task list. Watch a task appear the moment it is added"). A sentence spoken over a blank page or a sign-in form is about something the viewer cannot see yet; Tada holds such a caption until the page it is about is on screen.
• Walk the happy path only — no edge cases, errors, or dead ends. Show the feature working.
• Before each meaningful action, add a `caption` step that talks around it calmly, saying what it is for or what to notice ("This keeps only what you sent"), not a play-by-play like "Now I click Save". If the user has their own wording or tone, use theirs. ALWAYS include captions: a silent demo is a bad demo.
• End on the visible result so the viewer sees the payoff (the new item on screen, the success toast, etc.).
• Keep it tight: aim for ~30–90 seconds total.
• Prefer `text` locators (visible labels) over brittle CSS `selector`s for click/hover — they survive DOM and class changes.

IT BECOMES THE FEATURE’S PROOF: name the feature with `feature` (or the title names it) and the app with `repo`. A journey that passes and checks something is saved under that feature, and Tada replays it on every pull request from then on. So write it to be replayed: open the app by its path, and check the result with `expect`.

VERIFY IT ACTUALLY WORKS (important — do not skip):
• After each key action, add an `expect` step asserting the result really happened — e.g. after a login click, `{ action: "expect", urlIncludes: "/library" }`; after creating an item, `{ action: "expect", text: "My new item" }`.
• `expect` supports `text` (visible text appears), `urlIncludes` (URL contains a substring), or `selector` (element becomes visible).
• If any `expect` fails, Tada will NOT upload the demo — it returns the failed checkpoints so you can fix the steps and re-record. This guarantees a published demo shows the feature actually working, not a stuck/blank screen.

SHOW THE WHOLE FEATURE, NOT ONE CLICK (archetype beats — docs/feature-archetypes.md):
• A feature demo is complete when a viewer could explain the feature back. Match the shape, then hit its beats:
• FILTER/SEARCH: the unfiltered list WITH ITS COUNT → apply → the changed list and count → clear, count restored. The count is the narration.
• CREATE: open → fill visibly → submit → THE NEW THING IN THE LIST (the beat thin demos skip). EDIT: change one field → the change visible where a viewer would look. DELETE: gone from the list.
• TABLE/LIST: say what a row is, open one, come back; sort a column if it sorts. SETTINGS: flip it, then SHOW THE CONSEQUENCE somewhere else — a toggle never shown doing anything is a meaningless beat.
• WIZARD: every step is a landmark — show it, say its job, advance; end somewhere real. EMPTY STATE: what a new account sees, and doing what it suggests.
• HUMAN-ONLY (OAuth, "Connect Railway"): do not skip and never fake. `hover` the control and let the caption say what it does and what the person will see.

PROVE A FIX LIKE A QA, NOT A SCRIPT (when the demo answers "does X work?" or a bug report):
• Do not stop at the single assertion. "Click the thing, it works" PROVES it but does not EARN BELIEF. Plan a short tour of the adjacent states a real tester would check — all of them WORKING states (still the happy path, not edge cases or errors).
• Example — report: "overdue items still show after filtering by Sent". Filter Sent and `expect` the Sent-only result (the fix), THEN flip to a sibling filter (Overdue still lists them, All shows both), then back to Sent — showing the fix holds across the filter space, not just once.
• OBSERVE every tour step with its own `expect` — never aimless clicking. Conscious, not chaotic: author the whole tour up front; do NOT improvise random interactions (an automated demo that wanders can trip an UNRELATED bug on camera, or record differently each run).
• Keep the load-bearing checkpoint sacred: assert something that was FALSE before the fix and TRUE after. That single `expect` is the proof; the tour is the conviction around it — it never replaces or weakens it.

NARRATION (captions / voice-over):
• Narration is controlled ENTIRELY by the USER'S TADA SETTINGS (their dashboard Captions + Voice-over + voice toggles). There is no agent override — just write good captions; whether they're shown, spoken (and in which voice) is applied automatically from the account.

DRAG-AND-DROP: use a `drag` step to demo a drag UI (kanban board, reorderable list). Source is `selector`/`text` (like click); drop target is `toSelector`/`toText`. Example: `{ action: "drag", text: "My card", toText: "In Progress" }` moves a card between columns. It tries a pointer drag first (dnd-kit / react-beautiful-dnd) and auto-switches to native HTML5 drag events for real `draggable="true"` UIs — set `native: true` to force that. ALWAYS follow a `drag` with an `expect` asserting the item landed (e.g. `{ action: "expect", ... }`) — an unverified drag can silently no-op and must not publish.
VIEWPORT: set `device` to "desktop" (default), "mobile", or "tablet" to match the feature — use "mobile" only for mobile-first UIs.

RECORD AUTHED PAGES (login off-camera): wrap the sign-in in `pause`/`resume` — the browser still performs those steps but no frames are captured, so credentials never appear on screen and the demo starts clean on the authed page. Pattern: `{pause}` → goto /login → fill email/password → click "Sign in" → goto the page → `{resume}` → caption + demo.
⚠ NEVER TYPE A REAL PASSWORD INTO A STEP. The journey is stored on the run, so a literal credential would be written into our database in the clear. Type `{{secret.TADA_TEST_EMAIL}}` and `{{secret.TADA_TEST_PASSWORD}}` instead: the runner substitutes them from the app's test account at the moment it drives, and the stored journey keeps the placeholder. If the app has no test account yet, call `setup_test_account` once.

TADA KEEPS THE JOURNEY, NEVER THE REPOSITORY. Do not write any file into this repository for Tada. When a run PASSES, Tada keeps the journey it just verified as a journey of its feature, inside Tada, and replays it against every future pull request, so a change that breaks this feature fails its check. Tell the user the feature is now guarded. The demo proves the feature once; the kept journey re-proves it on every pull request.
• A failing run keeps nothing, by design: a guard built from a journey that did not work would lock in the breakage.
• For a feature built from a ticket, call plan_feature first, show the developer the plan, then send every journey of it here with `journeys` and the `feature` plan_feature returned.

captureScale.description: Shoot at 2 ONLY when this demo will be re-cut as marketing footage. A cut of 1x footage is capped at a 1.2x push-in forever, because the pixels for a closer look were never captured; 2 lifts that to 2.2x. It is a record-time decision that cannot be taken later, and it costs four times the frame pixels, so leave it off for an ordinary verification run.

device.description: Viewport preset — 'desktop' (default), 'mobile', or 'tablet'. Use 'mobile' only for mobile-first features.

dryRun.description: DEPRECATED AND IGNORED. This does NOT keep the recording local and does NOT skip the upload: every run happens on Tada and is published to a public link. Local recording no longer exists. If the app under test must not be published, do not run it here.

feature.description: The feature this proves, named exactly as the ticket (for example "Users, invitations and permissions"). Omit it and the title names the feature.

height.description: NOT SUPPORTED, and passing it refuses the run. Use `device`.

hideSelectors.description: CSS selectors for the app's own floating widgets to hide for the whole recording: a chat bubble, a feedback tab, a cookie banner. Nothing is hidden unless you pass this. Each match, and everything inside it, is removed with display:none on every page of the run. A step that clicks, types into, hovers, drags, scrolls to or waits for anything inside a hidden element FAILS the run and names the selector, so hide only what the journey never touches. Match the widget's container in the page itself: a selector cannot reach inside the widget's iframe or shadow root. Common containers (check them against your app, vendors change their markup): Intercom .intercom-app, .intercom-lightweight-app; HubSpot chat #hubspot-messages-iframe-container; Zendesk messaging iframe[title*="Zendesk"], iframe[aria-label*="Zendesk"]; Crisp #crisp-chatbox; Sentry user feedback #sentry-feedback; Userback .userback-button-container; Hotjar [class^="_hj"]; OneTrust cookie banner #onetrust-consent-sdk; Cookiebot cookie banner #CybotCookiebotDialog.

initScript.description: JavaScript run in every page BEFORE the app's own scripts, to seed state the app reads at boot. Use it to force a locale or a feature flag — e.g. "localStorage.setItem('lang','en')" for an app that would otherwise render in another language.

journeys.description: For a feature planned with plan_feature: every journey of the confirmed plan, named exactly as the plan names it, each with its steps. Send with feature set to the id plan_feature returned.

repo.description: The app this proves, as "owner/name". Left out, Tada reads it from the git remote of the folder this server was started in, which is wrong whenever that is not the app.

steps.description: Ordered actions to perform & record. Leave out when sending journeys for a planned feature, or when re-running a feature by name.

ms.description: wait/caption/scroll: milliseconds (scroll: animation duration); expect: max ms to wait for the condition (default 8000); awaitEmail: max ms to wait for the email (default 20000)

native.description: drag: force the synthetic HTML5 drag-and-drop path (real dragstart/dragover/drop events) for native `draggable="true"` UIs. Auto-detected when the source is draggable; set true only if auto-detect misses. Leave unset for pointer-based libraries (dnd-kit, react-beautiful-dnd).

selector.description: CSS selector for click/fill/hover/expect; select: combobox trigger; scroll: element to scroll to; drag: the source element to pick up

signedIn.description: expect: assert this page is past the sign-in: its address is not a sign-in address and no password box is showing. Use after opening a page only a signed-in person can see

text.description: click/hover/waitForText/expect: visible text to match (prefer over brittle CSS selectors); fill: label text; select: combobox label; caption: banner text; awaitEmail: subject substring to filter on; drag: visible text of the source to pick up

toSelector.description: drag: CSS selector of the drop target to drag the source ONTO

toText.description: drag: visible text of the drop target to drag the source ONTO

url.description: goto: URL to navigate to. May use ${magicLink} to open the link from the last awaitEmail.

urlIncludes.description: expect: assert the current URL contains this substring (e.g. "/library" to confirm a login worked)

value.description: fill: text to type (use ${inbox} for the disposable inbox address); select: the option to pick from a dropdown/combobox; scroll: 'top' | 'bottom' | pixel offset

storageState.description: NOT SUPPORTED, and passing it refuses the run rather than ignoring it. It names a file on YOUR machine and the run is driven by Tada's runner. To record a page behind a login, sign in inside the journey: see RECORD AUTHED PAGES below.

taskId.description: NOT SUPPORTED, and passing it refuses the run. Attach the published demo to a task from the dashboard.

ticket.description: The ticket id exactly as the tracker writes it, for example SOL-123. Lets Tada match the pull request that ships this feature.

title.description: Demo title, shown on the watch page

width.description: NOT SUPPORTED, and passing it refuses the run. Use `device`.

name: verify_feature
